sources.outlet: National Taxpayer Advocate (2012 Annual Report to Congress, Most Serious Problem)
sources.quote: identified more than 2,270 cases in which an organization was erroneously listed as having had its exempt status revoked
sources.searcher_note: COULD NOT OPEN: site redirects every fetch (WebFetch and curl) to a blank CloudFront page. Quote comes from the search tool's extract, not a page read; the checker must verify it. Extract says TIGTA found a programming problem and the most common cause was group-return subordinates not recognized; about 2011-12 wave

sources.quote: If an organization on the Auto-Revocation List has documentation that it met its filing requirement for one or more years during the three year period, what should it do?
sources.searcher_note: IRS FAQ acknowledging listed organizations may have filed in the three-year window; explainer, no counts. Date is page last-reviewed

sources.quote: In a random sample of 40 recently revoked 501(c)(3)s, 19 still had a full Form 990 filing history on the public record.
sources.searcher_note: Vendor marketing for a lookup tool; says revoked charities often show 990 filings (Truechild Inc revoked 2025-11-15 with 12 years of 990s). Does not say the returns fell in the missed years; the org may simply have stopped filing

sources.quote: Spencer told the Los Angeles Times on Monday that an IRS error was to blame for the National Policy Institute's failure to file federal tax returns.
sources.searcher_note: Single case where a revoked group blamed an IRS error; claim by the organization, not a finding

sources.outlet: Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (Report 2026-1S0-042)
sources.quote: The automatic revocations increased by approximately 59 percent from FY 2021 through FY 2025.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Volume context only (35,868 in FY2021 to 56,932 in FY2025); says nothing about revocations of organizations that had filed. Quote read from the PDF's extracted text

notes: No source found that names the 108 organizations, or any count of auto-revocations where a return from the missed years sits in the IRS e-file index, for 2019-2026. The closest pattern finding is the Taxpayer Advocate's 2012 report of 2,270+ erroneous listings from a programming problem (2011-12 wave), which could not be opened. Nothing found on revoked organizations 'quietly put back' without a recorded reinstatement. No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 on this error pattern.
